title: Typed custom properties
simpler: The syntax is inferred from the initial value, so one declaration replaces the five-line @property block, and the registration sits next to the rule that uses it.
differences: typed() registers with inherits: true. This @property uses inherits: false. When inheritance matters, write @property yourself.
Both are document-wide and permanent. typed() uses CSS.registerProperty(), the same registration @property performs.
typed() never overrides a native @property for the same name in a readable stylesheet.
typed() needs the runtime. Without it, --rotation stays an unregistered property and the rotation jumps instead of animating.
typed() is experimental. @property is native in current Chromium, WebKit and Firefox releases.
